plan: Store the workspace as a single deep-copied nested dict; all queries and mutations operate on this one tree, and to_data() returns a fresh deep copy.
Write two recursive helpers: _find(item_id) returning (containing_list, node) and _iter_items() yielding every node, so counting, marker collection, and move share one traversal strategy.
Compute note word counts by first deleting exact [[?identifier]] marker tokens with a regex, then counting \b\w+\b runs; references contribute their declared word_count.
Collect unresolved identifiers from note markers plus reference 'unresolved' lists into a set, returned sorted lexicographically.
Render outline() by depth-first walk: workspace title first, then each item at two spaces per nesting level as '<kind>: <title>'.

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: check id types, resolve source and destination, reject non-containers, reject self/descendant destinations via identity-based containment check, range-check the index against the destination length — only after all checks pass, remove (by identity) and insert. This guarantees failed moves leave the tree untouched.
Provide in-memory unittest cases (standard library only) covering totals, markers, outline text, successful moves with and without index, and every ValueError path with an unchanged-state assertion.
mechanisms: single deep-copied nested-dict tree as sole state
recursive parent-list lookup and full-tree iterator
regex marker stripping before \b\w+\b word counting
set-union then lexicographic sort for marker identifiers
depth-first outline rendering at two spaces per level
validate-before-mutate move with identity-based cycle/containment check
deep-copy snapshot on to_data() for isolation and failure-atomicity testing
